# FallForge Mint

> Bring one repetitive task and a few worked examples; walk out owning a real, private small model that does that job. FallForge Mint runs entirely in your browser: it turns your examples into a deterministic Ollama Modelfile you download and run on your own machine — a model you OWN, with no per-token bill and no data leaving your computer. Optional in-browser live preview (WebLLM, nothing to install). Every done-for-you mint carries a signed, re-checkable receipt that can — and sometimes does — say it LOST. Free to try. Published by AI-Native Solutions. MIT. ◊·κ=1.

## What it is

A self-contained tool for owning a specialised small model instead of renting a giant one per token. You describe one job, paste a handful of example inputs and correct answers, and the page assembles a real, byte-pinned Ollama Modelfile (system prompt + your examples baked in as few-shot). You run two commands (`ollama create`, `ollama run`) and own a private model that does that job on your own hardware. Honest scope: this is prompt-/few-shot tuning at the Modelfile level — a real, owned, reproducible node, not weight fine-tuning (that is the done-for-you tier).

## The three things it does, all in the browser

1. Mint — task + examples → a real downloadable Modelfile, with a SHA-256 fingerprint of the exact bytes.
2. Preview — optionally run a small model live in your browser (WebGPU/WebLLM) to see your node answer before installing anything.
3. Prove — re-verify a real signed mint receipt in your browser: it re-hashes the record and shows INTACT, and tampering one byte is caught. The shipped example (review-1b) BEATS its base by +31 points certified, and honestly LOSES to a model 7× its size.

## Re-run in CI

A scorecard made on the page can be downloaded as a re-run bundle: the signed receipt, the recipe and the held-out rows. The re-run rail (`.github/workflows/rerun.yml`, or the template repo fallforgemint-rerun) takes that bundle to a clean GitHub runner. There it recomputes every recorded number, and if the receipt names a CI run (its rerun link) it looks that run up on GitHub and checks the run made this exact receipt; any mismatch is TAMPERED and the job fails. GitHub keeps the run's artifact about 90 days; after that the rail confirms only that the run was the rail and was running when the receipt was stamped (RUN ONLY), never more. It then rebuilds the model with Ollama and runs the held-out set again: the same runtime must give the same hits (REPRODUCED), and a different runtime must give the same verdict (AGREES). Otherwise the result is DID_NOT_REPRODUCE, and the job fails. The verdict is a self-hashed attestation bound to the real run URL. It does not attest the machine that made the original, and it says nothing about what the base model saw in its own training.

## Own vs rent

An honest calculator: enter your monthly volume, tokens per call, and rented price per million tokens, plus your own one-off setup cost (hardware, time; 0 if you have the machine) and monthly run cost. It returns OWN_WINS, OWN_LATER, or RENT_WINS — it will tell you to keep renting when that is genuinely cheaper.

## Ways to work with us

- Do-it-yourself — free. Build, preview and download your Modelfile here; own it outright.
- Done-for-you — we mint, tune and prove one owned node with a signed receipt, and hand you a model you own.
- Run-it-for-you — we host, monitor and re-mint your nodes as your data changes.
- Regulated work (legal, tax, medical, financial products) is off the menu — counsel first.

## Privacy and ownership

Everything runs in your browser. Your task and examples are never sent anywhere. The model you build runs on your own machine and works offline. There is no account and no per-token bill.
